To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) termination of the relationship between the principal and the agent is optimal if and only if a cuto outside oer is reached; (ii) the size of the severance compensation, conditional on termination, depends positively on current compensation and negatively the agent’s current oer; and (iii) the optimal contract prescribes an inverted-U relationship of current compensation and the likelihood of termination.

(i) termination of the principal-agent relationship is optimal if and only if agent’s current outside opportunity is su ciently attractive, (ii) the size of the severance compensation is increasing in the agent’s current income and decreasing in the current outside oer, and (iii) the probability of termination is increasing in the current income and decreasing with the current outside opportunity.

the optimal contract prescribes that the principal should terminate the ongoing relationship with the agent if and only if his outside oer is above a cuto point, and that conditional on termination, the agent’s current pay and his outside oer are the two key determinants of the size of his severance compensation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal design of contracts that can be terminated and with the optimal timing of termination in the presence of costly termination and a stochastic outside oer.
the strategic interactions of the principal and the agent when the agent is subject to outside opportunities and the termination of the principal-agent relationship is costly.
the optimal dynamic contracting problem where the agent’s outside opportunities are stochastic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the model predicts a negative correlation between the agent’s outside opportunity and the probability of a costly termination of the ongoing relationship, which is consistent with the empirical evidence.
the optimal contract is such that the agent’s outside opportunity has a nonmonotonic eect on his compensation.
the optimal termination policy is a combination of the principal’s strategic response to the agent’s current oer with the agent’s optimal response to the principal’s optimal response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimal contract in our setting is characterized by an inverted-U relationship in the agent’s current wage, a U-shape relationship in the agent´s current outside offer and a negative relationship in the severance compensation.
the principal’s optimal contract is designed to balance the agent’s outside opportunity and the cost of termination.
the agent’s current wage is not the only determinant of the probability of termination, and the agent’s current oer also has an important impact on this probability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in the presence of costly termination and stochastic outside opportunities, the optimal contract may dictate that the agent’s current wage is negatively related to his current outside oportunity and that the optimal severance pay is zero.
the presence of costly termination, which is a key feature of the labor market, has a signicant eect on the principal-agent relationship and the optimal contract design.
the principal’s strategic response to the agent’s oer, which is absent in Burdett ( 1978), is crucial in determining the shape of the relationship between wages and tenure.
